title: "What do you do?" "My best.": the barely-coping caption
summary: A "Me when..." caption about a moment you're only just getting through, over the interview sound where the answer is "My best." AI writes the captions.
why: A trend tracker updated November 15, 2026 lists this as a fresh format with 229 creators that week: an interview sound asks "what do you do?", the answer is "my best", and the on-screen text starting with "Me when..." shows a situation the creator is barely coping with.
steps: Find the interview sound in your app by searching the line "what do you do? my best".
Paste the main prompt and pick the caption that feels most like your real week.
Film a short clip of yourself in that moment, or use one photo. A tired half-smile or a slow nod sells it.
Put the caption on screen for the whole clip and post. Keep the text short so it's easy to read.

prompts.label: Main prompt
prompts.text: Write 10 short on-screen captions for a video trend. Each caption starts with "Me when" and describes a small, everyday moment where I'm only just coping, so the joke is that I'm doing "my best". Base them on my real life: [describe your week, job, kids, pets, commute, school]. Keep each one under 15 words. Make them warm and relatable, not sad or mean. No hashtags, no emojis.

prompts.label: Variation: November in Canada
prompts.text: Write 8 "Me when..." captions about getting through November in Canada, where the joke is I'm doing my best. Use small moments like scraping the car at 7 a.m., the sun setting before 5 p.m., finding a matching pair of mitts, or the first slushy sidewalk. Each one under 15 words. Light and funny.

prompts.label: Variation: small business
prompts.text: I run [type of business]. Write 8 "Me when..." captions about busy-season moments where I'm doing my best, like [a few real examples: the holiday rush, the printer jamming, three orders at once]. Each under 15 words. Make customers smile and feel they know us. Keep it kind to customers. Don't make up sales numbers, reviews or customer quotes.

tips: Pick a moment people see themselves in. Small and specific beats big and dramatic.
Let your face do the work. A calm, slightly frazzled look is funnier than a big reaction.
Keep it light. This trend is about getting by with a smile, not about real distress.
Only show people who have said yes.
